title: Sentence Rearrangement Within Paragraphs
tagline: Year 3 — Four jumbled sentences between a fixed opening and a fixed closing sentence

introduction.overview: In this format the first and last sentences of a paragraph are given (S1 and S6), and four sentences in between, labelled P, Q, R and S, are jumbled. The fixed ends make the task easier than a full jumble, because S1 tells you what the paragraph is about and S6 tells you where it must arrive. The job is to build the bridge between them.
introduction.placementRelevance: Sentence-rearrangement items with S1 and S6 given are a classic of verbal sections in campus and bank tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Fitting new points into the middle of a drafted document uses the same cues.

learningObjectives: Use S1 to predict what must come first
Use S6 to predict what must come last
Link middle sentences by pronouns and time words
Check the order by reading S1 to S6 in one go
Eliminate options using one reliable link

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Look for sentences that begin with a reference (he, it, this, there) or a time word (at first, later, within a few decades).

coreDefinitions: S1 and S6: the given first and last sentences.
Bridge: the four middle sentences that connect S1 to S6.
Link: a word or idea connecting two adjacent sentences.
Anchor link: a link so strong that it settles the position of two sentences.
Chronological order: events in the order they happened.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: S1 poses a topic and S6 gives a result. The middle tells how you got from one to the other, usually in time or cause order.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Read S1 and S6 first. Predict the first middle sentence by asking what S1 leads to. Then link the others by time words and pronouns.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Prediction
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: S1 leads to the first middle sentence

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Reference link
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: "He" follows the sentence that names him

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Time words
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: At first → within a few decades → today

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Closing check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: S6 follows naturally from the last middle sentence

mainNarrative: S1: "The marathon takes its name from a Greek legend." The natural next sentence is the story ("According to the story, a messenger ran…"). Then "He covered about forty kilometres" needs the messenger; "On arrival he delivered his message" needs the journey; "When the modern Olympic Games began…" moves from the legend to the modern race; S6 gives the final distance.

S1: "Tea was discovered… by accident." The accident comes first (the leaves drifting into the pot), then the emperor tasting it, then the news spreading, then the Tang dynasty, then the Silk Road in S6.

S1: "Compound interest is often called the most powerful idea…" The simple-interest definition comes first so that "Under compound interest" can contrast with it. "In the early years the difference between the two is small" follows both definitions. "Over several decades, however…" contrasts with the early years and leads to S6.
Use one anchor first. "He covered about forty kilometres" must follow the sentence naming the messenger; once that pair is fixed, the others fall into place.
Finally, read S1, then the order, then S6. A jump in sense means a pair is wrongly placed.

deepDiveAspects.title: Contrast pairs
deepDiveAspects.content: "Under simple interest… Under compound interest…" is a contrast pair: define the baseline first.

deepDiveAspects.title: Time words
deepDiveAspects.content: "At first", "within a few decades" and "now" give a time ladder; place them in order.

solvedExamples.title: First middle sentence
solvedExamples.question: S1: "The marathon takes its name from a Greek legend." Which sentence follows: "According to the story, a messenger ran from the battlefield at Marathon to Athens" or "He covered about forty kilometres without rest"?

steps.title: Choice
steps.explanation: The first sentence tells the story; "He" needs the messenger first.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: According to the story, a messenger ran from the battlefield at Marathon to Athens
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The second sentence needs the first.

solvedExamples.title: Contrast link
solvedExamples.question: In a paragraph on interest, which comes first: "Under simple interest, you earn a fixed amount each year" or "Under compound interest, interest earned is added to the balance"?

steps.title: Baseline
steps.explanation: Simple interest is the base case.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Under simple interest, you earn a fixed amount each year

solvedExamples.title: Closing check
solvedExamples.question: After "The telephone changed the pace of commerce and of family life alike" which fits as S6: "Its descendant, the mobile phone, now fits in a pocket" or "In 1876 Bell patented a device"?

steps.title: Time
steps.explanation: The mobile phone is the latest stage.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Its descendant, the mobile phone, now fits in a pocket
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The patent belongs at the start.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Predict the first middle sentence from S1, link pairs by pronouns and time words, and check the result against S6.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Check that the order arrives at S6.
The first middle sentence names its subject.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Use the first-sentence prediction to drop half of the options.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Find one anchor pair and build around it.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Time words are the most reliable links.

easy.question:
The first and the last sentences of a paragraph are given as S1 and S6. The four middle sentences are jumbled.
S1. The marathon takes its name from a Greek legend.
P. On arrival he delivered his message and then collapsed.
Q. According to the story, a messenger ran from the battlefield at Marathon to Athens to announce a victory.
R. When the modern Olympic Games began in 1896, organisers recalled the story and added a long race to honour it.
S. He covered about forty kilometres without rest.
S6. The distance was later fixed at 42.195 kilometres, and it has not changed since 1921.

Which of the following gives the correct order of P, Q, R and S?
easy.explanation: The correct order is QSPR. S1 introduces the subject; each middle sentence then picks up the one before it by time or reference, and S6 draws the conclusion.

easy.explanation: The correct order is QSPR. So the sentence that follows S1 is Q.

intermediate.question:
The first and the last sentences of a paragraph are given as S1 and S6. The four middle sentences are jumbled.
S1. Tea was discovered, according to Chinese tradition, by accident.
P. He tasted the infusion and found it refreshing.
Q. By the Tang dynasty tea had become a national drink, with its own etiquette and its own poets.
R. Emperor Shennong was boiling drinking water when a few leaves from a nearby bush drifted into the pot.
S. Word of the new drink spread through the court, and cultivation of the bush began.
S6. Traders later carried it along the Silk Road, and from there it reached the rest of the world.

Which sentence follows S1 most logically?
intermediate.explanation: The correct order is RPSQ. So the sentence that follows S1 is R.

advanced.question:
The first and the last sentences of a paragraph are given as S1 and S6. The four middle sentences are jumbled.
S1. Compound interest is often called the most powerful idea in personal finance.
P. Over several decades, however, the compounding balance pulls far ahead.
Q. Under compound interest, the interest earned in one year is added to the balance and itself earns interest in later years.
R. In the early years the difference between the two is small.
S. Under simple interest, you earn a fixed amount each year on the money you first deposited.
S6. This is why starting to save early matters more than saving large amounts later.

Which sentence is third in the correct order of P, Q, R and S?
advanced.explanation: The correct order is SQRP. So the third sentence is R.

advanced.question:
The first and the last sentences of a paragraph are given as S1 and S6. The four middle sentences are jumbled.
S1. Before the telephone, urgent news travelled only as fast as a person or a telegraph wire could carry it.
P. Within a few decades, however, businesses had installed telephones, and exchanges connected whole cities.
Q. The telephone changed the pace of commerce and of family life alike.
R. At first many people saw it as a curiosity rather than a tool.
S. In 1876 Alexander Graham Bell patented a device that could carry the human voice along a wire.
S6. Its descendant, the mobile phone, now fits in a pocket and has made the wire unnecessary.

Which of the following gives the correct order of P, Q, R and S?
advanced.explanation: The correct order is SRPQ. S1 introduces the subject; each middle sentence then picks up the one before it by time or reference, and S6 draws the conclusion.
